name: raw-and-custom-pass-through
description: RAW and an unrecognised CUSTOM name are protocol-legal traffic, not unrecognised material: the run completes and nothing warns
kill: route RAW or an unrecognised CUSTOM name through the unrecognised-material path in enforceEvents (take "RAW"/"CUSTOM" out of the recognised set, so `!isRecognizedEvent` warns and returns `EMPTY`) — the escape hatch is then both complained about, which `noWarnings` catches, and swallowed, which `eventTypes` catches. RAW and CUSTOM being PRESENT in the delivered list is the whole point of this fixture: they are legal traffic a consumer must actually receive, and without the list a client that warned and dropped them would still pass every other key here.

dotnet.intentional: The .NET client's event surface is ChatResponseUpdate.RawRepresentation, and the builder-only events yield no update: TEXT_MESSAGE_START and TEXT_MESSAGE_END open and close the message being assembled and hand a consumer nothing, so they cannot appear in a delivered list however faithfully the client processes them. The list here is the base list minus exactly those; every event this fixture is actually about is still in it, in order. RAW and CUSTOM — the escape hatches this fixture exists to prove a consumer actually receives — are both in it, so the assertion still bites here.
